**Friday deploys to production are allowed, but they require approval from the on-call engineering manager.**

The standard deployment window is **Monday through Thursday, 09:00–16:00 Pacific**. Outside that window—including Friday afternoons—you need explicit sign-off from the on-call engineering manager before pushing to prod [1].

**Quick checklist if you need a Friday deploy:**
1. Get approval from the on-call engineering manager (the current rotation is in PagerDuty / the team directory).
2. The change still goes through the normal canary process (5% of traffic, auto-promoted after 20 minutes if error rates and p95 latency stay within 10% of baseline) [1].
3. If the change is a “normal” or “emergency” production change per the approval policy, follow those additional sign-off steps [2].

Rollbacks are always permitted at any time without approval [1].

**No.** Halcyon Health policy explicitly prohibits pasting any patient details into public chatbots or general-purpose AI assistants—even if you remove the patient's name.

**Key reasons:**

- **Removing a name is not enough.** The policy states: *"'De-identified' is not a loophole: removing a name is not enough to make a case non-identifiable, so treat any patient details as PHI."* [1]
- **Public chatbots are not approved.** The approved AI tools list categorically excludes *"Public chatbots and general-purpose AI assistants, on any device, including personal phones."* [1]
- **PHI may only go into approved systems.** The HIPAA privacy policy says: *"PHI may only be stored in the EHR, the practice management system, and approved Halcyon systems listed on the intranet. Never put PHI in … AI tools that are not on the approved list."* [2]
- **Even Halcyon's own internal assistant (Halcyon Assist) is marked "PHI allowed? No" with the condition: "Policy questions only. Do not paste patient details, even without names."** [1]

**What you can do instead:**
- Use the **Meridian EHR** for clinical documentation and summaries.
- If you need AI-assisted summarization, the only approved tool that handles PHI is **Quillon Ambient** (AI scribe), and it is limited to pilot clinics (Riverside and Elm Park) with patient verbal consent and clinician review. [1]
- For policy questions, use **Halcyon Assist**—but only for policies, never for patient data. [1]

If you believe a new AI tool should be evaluated for clinical use, contact the Privacy Officer (Margaret Holloway) and the HIPAA Security Officer (Ahmed Siddiqui); the review process typically takes 6–10 weeks. [1]

**287 workspaces** received duplicate invoices, and **$184,300** was refunded across **201 auto-charged invoices** [1].

**Details from the incident (INC-2340):**
- The month-end invoicing job ran twice for some workspaces, creating 312 duplicate September invoices across 287 workspaces [1].
- Of those, 201 invoices were auto-charged to customers on card auto-pay [1].

**17 lab results** were filed into the wrong patient's chart during the Bayline incident (July 21–23, 2026) [1].

**Why it happened:**  
On July 20, Bayline Reference Laboratories deployed a change to its results feed that moved the medical record number (MRN) into a different HL7 segment **without notifying Halcyon Health**. When the interface engine (Switchyard) could no longer locate the MRN, it fell back to a secondary matching rule that used only **last name and year of birth**. That fallback rule had existed since 2021 but had never been exercised at volume, so 100% of Bayline results were matched incorrectly for three days until a medical assistant at Riverside spotted a mismatch on July 23 [1].

**Contributing factors identified in the root-cause analysis:**
- No monitoring or alerting when results were matched via the fallback rule.
- The Bayline services agreement did not require advance notice of feed-format changes.
- The name-and-birth-year fallback was removed afterward, and alerts for fallback usage were added [1].
cited_titles: Root cause analysis: lab results filed to the wrong patient chart (RCA-26-07)

**Yes, Northwind Labs has a comparable mechanism called "Emergency access to customer workspaces," but it's designed for technical support incidents rather than clinical care.** Here's how the two differ:

| Aspect | Halcyon Health (Break-the-glass EHR) | Northwind Labs (Emergency workspace access) |
|--------|--------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------|
| **Purpose** | Access patient charts outside your assigned panel when care genuinely requires it (unscheduled urgent visit, covering a colleague, telehealth escalation) [1] | Access a customer's workspace only for an open support case or declared incident [3] |
| **Prior approval** | **None** — patient care comes first; you break the glass yourself and justify it afterward [1] | **Required** — a second engineer (not on the same case) must approve the request in Teleport before access is granted [3] |
| **Duration** | Until end of your shift, up to **12 hours** [1] | **2 hours** (deliberately shorter than the standard 8-hour Teleport session) [3] |
| **Access level** | Full chart access for care | **Read-only by default**; write access (e.g., editing a pipeline) needs the customer's written consent in the case first [3] |
| **Audit & review** | Every event logged; Privacy Officer's team reviews within **2 business days**; manager asked to confirm if reason unclear [1] | All sessions **recorded and kept 1 year**; workspace audit log shows access with case ID; enterprise admins emailed within **24 hours**; Security reviews a weekly sample + every write-access session [3] |
| **Prohibited uses** | Checking family, coworkers, public figures, or yourself — terminable offense under HIPAA [1][5] | "Curiosity," "it would be faster," accessing a workspace of someone you know personally, exporting payloads, or screen-sharing the session [3] |
| **Underlying system** | Meridian EHR (clinical records) | Teleport (production/customer workspaces) [3][4] |

**In short:** Halcyon's break-the-glass is a **clinician-initiated, retrospective-review** model optimized for urgent patient care. Northwind's emergency access is a **dual-approval, time-boxed, heavily recorded** model optimized for protecting customer data during support incidents.
cited_titles: HIPAA privacy and PHI handling policy

**365 days** is the current default retention period for customers' archived event data.

The current standard (v2.0, effective September 15, 2026) specifies that archived event payloads stored in Driftwood (the cold store) are kept for **365 days** by default [2]. This reduced the previous v1 default of 400 days [2].

Enterprise customers can contract for longer retention (up to 730 days) with security team approval, but the standard default remains 365 days [2].
